FN-QPVB555-1
FISCAL NOTE
Senate Bill 60
Committee: Finance and Taxation General Fund Sponsor: Senator Arthur Orr
Analyst: Jennifer Farish Date: 02/13/2024
Senate Bill 60 as introduced would increase the administrative obligations of the Alabama
Department of Economic and Community Affairs to facilitate and coordinate the development,
improvement, maintenance and construction of inland ports and transfer facilities via a grant
program established to finance improvements to existing publicly-owned inland ports and
intermodal facility infrastructure. To finance the grant program, this bill would require a transfer
a maximum of $5,000,000 annually from the Public Road and Bridge Fund to the Inland Ports
and Intermodal Development Fund established pursuant to the provisions of this bill. This bill
further provides for: (1) monies transferred into the fund that are unspent at the end of a fiscal
year to be carried forward for use in the next fiscal year and used to reduce the transfer for the
upcoming fiscal year such that the grant program shall not have available more than $5 million
in any single fiscal year; (2) grants to be awarded on a competitive bid basis with priority given
to certain inland ports and intermodal facilities; and (3) a minimum participation of 20% of
local funds for any project.

FN-QPVB555-2
FISCAL NOTE
Senate Bill 60
Committee: Finance and Taxation General Fund Sponsor: Senator Arthur Orr
Analyst: Jennifer Farish Date: 04/17/2024
Senate Bill 60 as reported by the Committee on Finance and Taxation General Fund would
increase the administrative obligations of the Alabama Department of Economic and
Community Affairs to facilitate and coordinate the development, improvement, maintenance
and construction of inland ports and transfer facilities via a grant program established to finance
improvements to existing publicly-owned inland ports and intermodal facility infrastructure. To
finance the grant program, this bill would require an appropriation from the State General Fund
of $2,000,000 annually beginning in fiscal year 2026 and continuing through the 2028 fiscal
year. This bill further provides for: (1) monies transferred into the fund that are unspent at the
end of a fiscal year to be carried forward for use in the next fiscal year and used to reduce the
transfer for the upcoming fiscal year such that the grant program shall not have available more
than $5 million in any single fiscal year; (2) grants to be awarded on a competitive bid basis
with priority given to certain inland ports and intermodal facilities; and (3) a minimum
participation of 20% of local funds for any project.

FN-QPVB555-3
FISCAL NOTE
Senate Bill 60
Committee: Ways and Means General Fund Sponsor: Senator Arthur Orr
Analyst: Jennifer Farish Date: 04/29/2024
Senate Bill 60 as passed the Senate would increase the administrative obligations of the
Alabama Department of Economic and Community Affairs (ADECA) to administer a grant
program to finance improvements to existing publicly-owned inland ports and intermodal
facility infrastructure which would be funded from the Inland Ports and Intermodal
Development Fund created by this bill within ADECA. This bill would also require an
appropriation from the State General Fund of $2,000,000 annually for fiscal years 2026, 2027,
and 2028. This bill further provides for: (1) monies in the fund that are unspent at the end of a
fiscal year to be carried forward for use in the next fiscal year and used to reduce the transfer for
the upcoming fiscal year such that the grant program shall not have available more than $5
million in any single fiscal year; except monies unexpended at the end of the third fiscal year
which shall revert to the State General Fund; (2) grants to be awarded on a competitive bid basis
with priority given to certain inland ports and intermodal facilities; and (3) a minimum
participation of 20% of local funds for any project.
